title: What trumpet players are easiest for a clarinetist
summary: A trumpeter who sticks to the melody is easier to play with than one who plays high bop-style notes.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: What I was wondering was if he was easy to work with.

I mean, would you say there was any particular kind of trumpet player that is easier to work with, like a man that stays and plays in the staff most of the time? Would you say it would be easier to play a clarinet with?
Well, yeah. A man that stays and is deaf and also a man that sticks to his melody. That makes it easier for the clarinet.
In other words, you say a man like some of these instruments play nowadays, they play all those high notes and that kind of bop stuff. You'd say that would be hard for a clarinet to play? Well, sure.
Yeah. I know it's hard for me. It's hard for you.
